answer: At enrollment, each identity locks a refundable token bond for its full horizon of work. Random task receipts place accounts into audit cohorts, such as the violet cohort; reviewers compare signed proofs and slash the bond when multiple identities reuse one operator's evidence. Honest agents get their bond back after the voyage, paying only the opportunity cost of locked capital, while an attacker must fund every persona and risks losing each bond. Thus adding Sybils raises both upfront capital and expected penalties.
